title: Fidelity susceptibility of Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model with further neighbour hopping term
abstract: In this study, topological phase transition in Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model with a further neighbour hopping term has been studied in terms of fidelity susceptibility. Topological phase transition point in the standard SSH model has been identified before by noting the divergence of fidelity susceptibility. The same approach has been employed here where fidelity susceptibility is found to diverge at the phase transition points. Additionally, effect of staggered potential on the fidelity susceptibility has been explored. Analytic expression for fidelity susceptibility has been obtained along with its numerical estimation on finite chains by exact diagonalization. Fidelity susceptibility exhibits sharp peaks at the phase transition points in both approaches. Scaling exponent of this divergence has been obtained numerically which is found to agree to that of the standard SSH model without further neighbour terms.
summary: This work applies fidelity susceptibility to study the topological phase transition in the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger model augmented with a further neighbour hopping term. The divergence of $\chi_f$ at critical points confirms the phase transition, and the scaling analysis shows the fundamental physics remains consistent with the standard SSH model. This provides a robust diagnostic tool for characterizing quantum critical points in 1D topological systems.
main_problem: The study investigates the topological phase transition in the Su-Schrieffer-Heeger (SSH) model when augmented with a further neighbour hopping term.
main_result: The fidelity susceptibility ($\chi_f$) is found to diverge at the phase transition points, and the scaling exponent obtained numerically agrees with that of the standard SSH model.
method: The analysis uses the fidelity susceptibility, derived from the overlap matrix of single-particle eigenstates, to detect quantum critical points.
model_or_system: The system is the SSH model, a 1D tight-binding model, extended by adding a further neighbour hopping term. The Hamiltonian is analyzed in both momentum space and for finite chains with open boundary conditions.
key_observables: Fidelity susceptibility ($\chi_f$), which is sensitive to parameter variations and diverges at phase transitions.
important_parameters: The control parameter is $\lambda = t/t'$, and the study explores the effect of staggered potentials ($\mu$) and the strength of the further neighbour hopping term ($t_0$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the non-interacting fermionic nature of the system, allowing the use of Slater determinants for calculating fidelity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy spectrum under different perturbations (staggered potential, FN hopping) and show the variation of $\chi_f(\lambda)$ near the transition points, demonstrating divergence.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the use of fidelity susceptibility to locate phase transitions in the standard SSH model. It then extends the analysis to include a further neighbour hopping term, deriving analytic and numerical expressions for $\chi_f$ to confirm the transition points and analyze scaling behavior.
why_interesting: The use of fidelity susceptibility as a diagnostic tool for topological phase transitions is a powerful, non-local measure applicable to many quantum systems, making it relevant for understanding critical points in condensed matter models.
